our_title: Worker generators seeded from the shared state while thread 0 is already drawing
ran: ThreadSanitizer (-O1 -fsanitize=thread, 4 threads) on pristine 7.0.17: 'WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race ... Write of size 8 by main thread: #0 _SCOTCHintRandVal3 common_integer.c:443 #1 _SCOTCHintRandVal #2 bgraphBipartGg2 bgraph_bipart_gg.c:196 ... Previous read by thread T3: #0 _SCOTCHintRandSpawn common_integer.c:296 #1 bgraphBipartGg2 bgraph_bipart_gg.c:177' (1 per run, 3/3 runs). Fresh-process determinism, SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=1, gpart 4 m16x16_b100000_v.grf, 30 runs: pristine thr=2 -> 3 distinct partitions (24/4/2), thr=4 -> 1 (racy side varies per run); after 0002 alone: thr=1/2/4 -> 1 distinct each but three different partitions (1d497d7d, d02c4de7, 944fb99a); after 0001-0004: thr=2/4/8 -> 1 distinct, all e180dfcf; 64-bit build the same. Patched TSan: 0 reports with SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=1 (5 runs), and with =0 only the intentional lock-free matching in graph_match_scan.c (5 runs). repro/SEP-13/README.
severity_note: Higher than the review's Medium: the race is reachable from the default strategy (bgraphBipartFm and bgraphBipartEx fall back to bgraphBipartGg) and breaks the documented contract of SCOTCH_OPTIONNUMDETERMINISTIC ('deterministic behavior across multiple runs, for any number of threads', s_l.tex:7900-7908), a 7.0.16 regression against 7.0.13-7.0.15.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/bgraph_bipart_gg.c:177 (spawn in worker), :196 (thread 0 draws), :308 and :328 (thread count / pass sharing ignore the deterministic option)
evidence: 177: intRandSpawn (grafptr->contptr->randptr, thrdnum, &randdat); /* Create fake local context */ ; 196: vexxptr = vexxtax + (grafptr->s.baseval + contextIntRandVal (contptr, grafptr->s.vertnbr)); ; common_integer.c:296: seedval = roldptr->statdat.randtab[0]; /* Get value from state of old generator */ ; 328: passdat.passnbr = (paraptr->passnbr + (thrdnbr - 1)) / thrdnbr; /* Share passes across threads */
review_accuracy: Mechanism, location and fix line are accurate. Incomplete for its own claim 'non-reproducible runs even in deterministic mode': spawning before the launch makes runs reproducible for a fixed thread count only; the documented contract is independence from the thread count, which needs the option to be honored (second commit).
first_pass_critique: Status and TSan evidence right; the sketch (spawn loop in the launcher, randdat in BgraphBipartGgThread) is what 0002 does. It called the deterministic-option half 'handled elsewhere by the parent' and never audited PyScotch's shipped patch; that patch is questioned here: (1) its '(descptr != NULL) ? threadNum (descptr) : 0' guard exists only because it calls bgraphBipartGg2 (NULL, ...) in the threaded build; the tree's idiom for 'deterministic => sequential' is graphMatch() (graph_match.c:286-291): launch all threads, non-zero threads return at once, so 0003 adds a working-thread count to BgraphBipartGgData instead and leaves the launch and the descriptor alone; (2) collapsing to one working thread is required (the doc promises thread-count independence), as PyScotch did, but through contextThreadNbr-sized tables, not by changing thrdnbr; (3) the '#include "context.h"' is needed (CONTEXTOPTIONNUMDETERMINISTIC lives there, as in graph_match.c:57); (4) contdat/contptr juggling stays: thread 0 must keep using the caller's context so that the sequential and deterministic results coincide (verified: thr=1 result unchanged, 1d497d7d, after the series). Its option 'derive the spawn seed from the stable seed' is wrong as written: successive calls in one context would give identical worker streams (alt/SEP-13-c, not recommended).

fix_options.label: a: spawn all local contexts in the launcher before contextThreadLaunch (0002) + honor the deterministic option the graphMatch way (0003)
fix_options.summary: 0002: IntRandContext randdat moves into BgraphBipartGgThread, the launcher spawns thrdtab[1..n-1].randdat sequentially, the worker uses &thrdptr->randdat. 0003: read CONTEXTOPTIONNUMDETERMINISTIC, store the number of working threads in BgraphBipartGgData.thrdnbr (1 if deterministic), share passes over it, non-working threads return at once with parttab = NULL (already the 'skip' marker of the reduction).
fix_options.tested: 32/64-bit builds 0 warnings; six check targets pass on both; TSan 0 reports (det=1) / only graph_match_scan.c (det=0); 30 fresh processes x {2,4,8} threads -> one partition each, identical across 2/4/8; debug build (-DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL) gpart 1 and 4 threads ok.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Non-deterministic mode: results now depend only on the thread count (same seeds as the first scheduling of pristine). Deterministic mode: GG runs on one thread (slower, as the doc says 'albeit sometimes slower'); idle threads cost a launch and a barrier. +32 bytes per thread in the internal thread block; no ABI change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: 0002 is the review's own fix and intRandSpawn's header comment already asks for it ('spawning can be performed in parallel ... The routine itself is not thread-safe'). 0003 copies graphMatchInit/graphMatch (graph_match.c:205-212, 286-291: 'Only thread 0 will perform the work') and the Gnum deteval + contextValuesGetInt idiom used in all three existing users of the option.

fix_options.label: b: PyScotch's shipped patch (collapse thrdnbr to 1 and call bgraphBipartGg2 (NULL, ...) directly)
fix_options.summary: Same pre-spawning, but when deterministic sets thrdnbr = 1, calls the thread routine with a NULL descriptor and guards threadNum() with 'descptr != NULL'.
fix_options.tested: Not re-run here; PyScotch reports 3 x 30 fresh processes, 2 and 4 threads, one partition (QUESTIONS_FOR_SCOTCH_TEAM.md). Behaviourally equivalent to (a) in deterministic mode.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Works, but introduces a NULL-descriptor convention in a threaded build that no other module has (NULL is only ever passed in *NOTHREAD builds where threadNum is not called), and a ternary on every thread entry.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would rewrite it into (a): graphMatch keeps the launch and lets non-zero threads return.

fix_options.label: c: make intRandSpawn seed from seedval instead of the live state
fix_options.summary: common_integer.c: seedval = roldptr->seedval, so spawning never reads mutable state.
fix_options.tested: compile-checked only (0 diagnostics); not run because it is wrong by design (see tradeoffs).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Race-free at every caller, but every call of bgraphBipartGg() in the same context gives worker k the same stream (seedval never changes), so all bipartitions of a recursive bisection would grow from the same root sequence; needs a per-context call counter, i.e. a new field in IntRandContext.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Changes the semantics of a common routine for one caller; he fixed callers, not common_integer.c, in this range.

fix_options.label: d: barrier inside the thread routine after spawning
fix_options.summary: Workers spawn first, all threads hit threadBarrier before any draw; spawn moved before the allocation so the barrier is reached on every path.
fix_options.tradeoffs: One more barrier per call; the barrier must stay before every early return (allocation failure) or the call deadlocks; does nothing for the deterministic option.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: More fragile than spawning in the launcher, where contextThreadLaunchSplit (common_context.c:298-299) already seeds the second sub-context before launching.

cleanup_done: 0002 removes the local 'IntRandContext randdat' of bgraphBipartGg2 and its worker-side intRandSpawn call; the 'Create fake local context' comment is replaced. intRandSpawn keeps its single caller (the launcher). Nothing else orphaned (git grep).
test_added: ; a '1 thread == N threads with the option set' test in test_scotch_context.c would be the natural home, but it fails on pristine+series for a reason outside this module (PS2-G08-2: kgraph_map_rb_part.c splits the context with a second random stream whenever >= 2 threads exist), so adding it would pin a contract the library does not yet meet; a same-thread-count reproducibility test would be flaky-detecting on pristine (fails in ~1 run of 5) and the maintainer does not ship probabilistic tests.
notes: Measured contract after the series: SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=1 gives one partition per thread count (30/30) and 2 == 4 == 8 threads; 1 thread still differs on some graphs because of PS2-G08-2 (not this module). Default/non-deterministic mode remains non-reproducible by design (lock-free matching).

our_title: All gain tables share one file-static sentinel link written by every thread
ran: TSan pristine 7.0.17, gpart 4 m16x16_b100000_v.grf, 4 threads: 14 of 19 reports per run are 'Write of size 8 ... #0 _SCOTCHgainTablAddLog gain.c:311 #1 bgraphBipartGg2 bgraph_bipart_gg.c:246 ... Previous write ... #0 bgraphBipartGg2 bgraph_bipart_gg.c:216 ... Location is global gainLinkDummy of size 24'; one report pairs bgraphBipartFm (bgraph_bipart_fm.c:524, gainTablDel macro) in one split sub-context with bgraphBipartGg2 in the other. Patched TSan (series): 0 reports in 5 deterministic runs, and no report in gain.c / bgraph_bipart_*.c in 5 non-deterministic runs nor in a bump.grf k=9 run. Debug build with -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_GAIN3 (exercises the new gainTablCheck signatures): gpart ok, check_scotch_graph_map/check_prog_gpart/check_scotch_context pass.
severity_note: The written field (prev of the sentinel) is never read, so no wrong result today; still a formal data race (UB), a shared cache line hammered by every thread's gain-table insert/delete (false sharing on a hot path), and it crosses independent split contexts, not only GG workers.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/gain.c:76 (static sentinel), :257 (gainTablAddLin write), :311 (gainTablAddLog write), :343 (gainTablDel write); gain.h:129 (gainTablDel macro writes it from every FM/GG module)
evidence: 76: static GainLink gainLinkDummy; /*+ Dummy link space for fast linked list operations +*/ ; 311: entrptr->next->prev = linkptr; /* Link vertex in gain list: TRICK */ ; 343: linkptr->next->prev = linkptr->prev; /* TRICK: may write in dummy link area */ ; gain.h:129: #define gainTablDel(tabl,link) (((GainLink *) (link))->next->prev = ((GainLink *) (link))->prev, ...
first_pass_critique: Right finding and right preferred option, but 'not compiled' and it missed that the write also happens through the gainTablDel macro in gain.h (bgraph_bipart_gg.c:216/245, bgraph_bipart_fm.c:524 in the TSan output), which decides between the options: a conditional write cannot be done in that macro without exporting the static sentinel (alt b shows the cost), and a thread-local sentinel breaks tables whose init and use are in different threads. It also missed the debug checkers gainTablCheck/gainTablCheck2 that need the table pointer once the sentinel is per table (caught here by compiling with -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_GAIN3).

fix_options.label: a: per-table dummy link embedded in GainTabl (linkdat)
fix_options.summary: GainTabl gets 'GainLink linkdat; /*+ Dummy link for fast list operations +*/'; gain.c compares against &tablptr->linkdat; the static is deleted; the debug checkers take the table pointer.
fix_options.tested: 32/64-bit builds 0 warnings; gain.c also compiled with -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_GAIN1/2/3; full -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_GAIN3 build runs gpart and three check targets; TSan clean for gain.c; six check targets pass on both widths.
fix_options.tradeoffs: +24 bytes per table; the branch-free TRICK is kept; writes now land in the owning table's memory; no behaviour change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: His own idiom: fibo.h:104 'FiboNode rootdat; /*+ Dummy node for fast root insertion +*/' with '!= &treeptr->rootdat' comparisons in fibo.c; keeps the gain.h macro untouched and the sentinel private.

fix_options.label: b: conditional writes, sentinel exported for the gain.h macro
fix_options.summary: Guard the three writes with 'if (x->next != &gainLinkDummy)'; the macro in gain.h needs the sentinel, so it becomes a non-static exported symbol (module.h rename) and the macro a do/while.
fix_options.tested: compile-checked only (gain.c and bgraph_bipart_gg.c with the modified gain.h, 0 diagnostics); not run.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Adds a branch on the hottest path of every FM/GG (the TRICK exists to avoid it), exports a new internal symbol, changes a statement-expression macro into a do/while that no longer composes in expressions.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Defeats the explicit 'TRICK' design comment; he would not add a branch there.

fix_options.label: c: thread-local sentinel
fix_options.tradeoffs: Two lines, but pointer identity differs per thread: a table initialized by one thread (entries = &dummy_A) and used by another compares against &dummy_B and sees every slot as non-empty; needs C11 or compiler extensions (_Thread_local / __declspec(thread)), which the tree does not use anywhere.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Introduces a portability dependency and a latent semantic trap for a 24-byte saving.

cleanup_done: Removes the file-static gainLinkDummy and its 'static variables' section; nothing else references it (git grep: only gain.c; module.h never renamed it). Also removes a pre-existing trailing-whitespace line in gainTablMove (gain.c:457 '}     ') flagged by stylecheck.py.
test_added: ; no natural home: src/check has no gain-table unit test and the defect is only visible under ThreadSanitizer.
notes: The race also exists between the two sub-contexts of kgraphMapRbPart (FM in one, GG in the other), so it predates 7a934a8 for any strategy running two bipartitions concurrently; 0004 covers all users since every table now owns its sentinel.
